title: Juggling Bean Bags (set of 4)
summary: Four little filled squares for juggling and throwing games — sew by hand or machine.
description: The best first project for kids learning to sew with an adult: tiny seams, instant results. Use felt or cotton scraps and fill with rice or plastic pellets.

materials.name: Sturdy cotton or felt scraps
materials.why: Bag fabric — tightly woven so filling can't escape.

materials.name: Filling
materials.quantity: About 120 g per bag (480 g total)

steps.title: Choose and press fabrics
steps.text: Pick four pairs of fabrics — mismatched pairs look fun. Press them.

steps.title: Cut eight squares
steps.text: Cut eight 12 cm squares (two per bean bag).
warnings: Children should only use scissors with adult supervision.

steps.title: Sew around three and a half sides
steps.text: Place two squares right sides together. Sew all round with a 1 cm seam, leaving a 4 cm gap on one side. By hand, use a small backstitch so the filling can't escape.
steps.beginner: Backstitch by hand: bring the needle up, take a stitch backwards, then come up a stitch-length ahead. Keep stitches about 3 mm long.

steps.title: Clip and turn
steps.text: Clip the corners, turn right side out and poke the corners out gently.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Use a funnel to fill each bag about ¾ full — around 120 g. Leave room so it stays floppy for juggling.
warnings: Small parts and fillings are a choking hazard — not for children under 3.

steps.title: Close the gap
steps.text: Fold the gap's edges in and ladder-stitch it closed with small, firm stitches.

steps.title: Play!
steps.text: Make all four and try a three-ball cascade.

review.note: Sample pattern; dimensions are internally consistent but not yet test-sewn.
